content.text:
I submitted **index 23 (Cr0.21Sb0.79)** as the best composition. Its measured EQE was **0.0161%**, the highest of the three merit measurements. All the EQE values are small, so this is only the best of three points on the composition line.

| Index | Cr fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | 0.51 (CrSbO4) | 0.0033 |
| 23 | 0.21 | **0.0161** |
| 27 | 0.13 | 0.0083 |

- **Where it peaks:** EQE was lowest at 50:50 and rose about fivefold on the Sb-rich side. It then dropped again at the most Sb-rich point, so the best composition is probably somewhere around 15–25% Cr. The composition next to index 23 (index 22 or 24) might be slightly better, but none were left to measure.
- **Not explored:** I never measured the Cr-rich end (indices 0–8). I skipped it because the 50:50 result was poor and the trend pointed the other way, so a good composition there can't be ruled out.
- **Structure:** XRD on indices 13 and 19 both matched a rutile-type pattern.
- **Model predictions:** They didn't help much. The predicted band gaps ranged from about 0.9 to 2.0 eV, all below the 2.4 eV light, so they didn't tell the compositions apart. The known mixed Cr–Sb phases all sit slightly above the stable limit (about 0.06–0.11 eV/atom).

I used all 3 merit measurements and 2 of the 5 XRD measurements.
